sentences.text: THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO ALLOW THE APPEAL, THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.03.2022 PASSED IN MVC NO.23/2021 BY THE LEARNED MEMBER MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL-II, YADGIR MAY KINDLY BE MODIFIED BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AS CLAIMED IN THE CLAIM PETITION, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
This is claimants appeal questioning the quantum determined by the Tribunal in MVC.No.23/2021.
The appeal is purely on quantum since Insurance company admits its liability.
2. The appellants filed a claim petition for having lost one Ramappa in a road traffic accident dated NC: 2024:KHC-K:9519 21.12.2020.

The appellants contended that deceased was doing agricultural work and was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
3.
The Tribunal answered issue No.1 in the affirmative and proceeded to determine compensation.
In absence of income proof, the Tribunal notionally assessed the income at Rs.10,000/- and awarded Rs.11,43,948/- by adding 10% future prospects.
The Tribunal in all awarded a sum of Rs.13,33,948/-.
4. Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellants.

Learned counsel appearing for the Corporation strongly objected not to consider 25% future prospects on the ground that deceased was aged 50 years and therefore, 10% future prospects determined by the Tribunal is just and proper.

sentences.text: On meticulous reading of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and NC: 2024:KHC-K:9519 Ors.1, the wordings clearly reveal that upto age 40, 40% has to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and NC: 2024:KHC-K:9519
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, since appellant is aged 50 years, this Court is inclined to take 25% towards future prospects and not 10% as argued by the learned counsel appearing for the Corporation.
6. The appellants have not produced any documentary evidence to substantiate deceased income.
In absence of income proof, this Court is inclined to place reliance on the income chart prepared by the Legal Services Authority.
The accident is of the year 2020.
Accordingly, income is assessed at Rs.13,750/- and after adding 25% towards future prospects, income is taken at Rs.17,187.5/-.

After deducting 1/3rd and by applying the multiplier of 13, the compensation payable under the head 'loss of dependency' works out to Rs.17,87,500/- (17,187.5x12x13x2/3).
2017 ACJ 2700 SC NC: 2024:KHC-K:9519 7.
Since there are four dependents, Rs.1,90,000/- is awarded under conventional heads.

The accident is of the year 2020 and therefore, in the light of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.2, 10% escalation for every three years which works out to Rs.19,000/- is added under conventional heads.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The total compensation re-determined by this Court works out to Rs.19,96,500/- as against Rs.13,33,948/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
